strategy.reason: All 18 prior attempts (BOOTSTRAP through cycle 7) failed due to purely infrastructural causes (missing arguments, missing ContractValidationError symbol, CodeAgent.run attribute error, stale artifacts, smoke-test shape mismatch, Unicode encoding). No scientific evidence is yet available. The previous scientific ideas (linear operators with various priors, non-Markovian delay, divergence-free coordinates, multi-scale slow/fast splits, symplectic energy-preserving reduction, regime-conditioned Koopman, sparse symbolic + residual, Bayesian shrinkage, energy-band sparsity, non-modal transient growth, info-theoretic nonlinearity test, recurrence-conditioned operator, Lie-group equivariance, RKHS operator-valued kernels, graph-block decomposition, weak residual, implicit history, nonlinear lifting) have not been scientifically evaluated. We therefore generate three new hypotheses that introduce genuinely different mechanisms and target discriminative experiments that can be run on development_train/development_validation only, while remaining compatible with the 52D POD latent representation and the deterministic single-step rollout contract.

hypotheses.name: Invertible coordinate warping with global linear core (Normalizing-Flow Koopman)
hypotheses.scientific_question: Is the failure of fixed-coordinate linear operators caused by the POD coordinate system itself, so that an invertible nonlinear re-coordinatization of the same 52D latent would make the dynamics globally linear in the warped coordinates?
hypotheses.mechanism: Learn an invertible diffeomorphism phi: R^52 -> R^52 implemented as a normalizing flow (stack of affine coupling layers with 52D latent). In the warped coordinates w = phi(z), the dynamics are postulated to be exactly linear: w_{t+1} = A w_t. The full prediction is z_{t+1} = phi^{-1}(A phi(z_t)). A is a single fixed 52x52 matrix. The flow phi and A are trained jointly on development_train only.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: z_{t+1} = phi^{-1}(A * phi(z_t)), with phi = phi_K o ... o phi_1 composed of K affine coupling layers, each with elementwise invertible scalings and translations. Log-det-Jacobian is tractable. A is fit by least squares in warped coordinates after phi is fixed (alternating optimization). The operator acts in the warped (canonical) space, not in the raw POD space.
hypotheses.motivation: All prior linear-operator candidates (BOOTSTRAP_H1, C001_H01, C002_H02, C003_H01, C003_H02, C003_H03, C004_H01, C004_H03) and the RKHS candidate (cycle 6 H2) kept the raw 52D POD basis fixed and only modified the operator. If the true dynamics are linear but in a curved coordinate system (a common situation in fluid ROMs), no operator class acting in the raw POD basis can be globally accurate. Normalizing-flow Koopman attacks the representation rather than the operator, providing a clean discriminator between representation failure and operator-form failure. It is also genuinely different from the nonlinear-lifting fallback (H_fallback_lift), which proposed a non-invertible lift to higher dimensions; here we keep dimension fixed and require exact invertibility and a single global linear core.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: Prior attempts either (a) used fixed POD coordinates and only varied the operator (so a representation failure would look like an operator failure for all of them) or (b) proposed non-invertible lifts without a global linear core. The symmetric energy-preserving reduction (C002_H01) and divergence-free coordinates (C001_H02) also changed coordinates but imposed rigid physical constraints rather than a learnable invertible warp; if the true canonical coordinates are not strictly divergence-free or energy-preserving, those constraints would dominate the error. This hypothesis instead learns the warp from data while keeping the dynamics in the warped space as simple as possible (a single linear operator).
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If the dynamics are linear in some unknown but smooth coordinate system, this hypothesis will (i) achieve lower multi-step rollout error than any fixed-coordinate linear operator at matched parameter count, and (ii) the learned operator A in the warped space will have a near-constant residual when refit in held-out warped coordinates, whereas refitting a global linear operator in raw POD coordinates will show large state-dependent residuals. The Jacobian determinant of phi should be significantly non-unity in regions where prior operators underperform.
minimum_experiment: Split development_train into train/calibrate. Fit phi and A on development_train. Evaluate 1-step and N-step rollout RMSE on development_validation.
Compare against a baseline global linear operator (least-squares fit in raw POD) at matched parameter count.
Probe invertibility: pass z through phi then phi^{-1} and check reconstruction error on development_validation.
Diagnostic: refit a global linear operator in the warped coordinates and check residual structure; it should be near-zero if the hypothesis is correct.
Sensitivity sweep over the number of coupling layers K to verify the warp is not just adding capacity to a non-invertible model.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: Multi-step rollout RMSE on development_validation drops below the global linear baseline by a clear margin, and the reconstruction error phi(phi^{-1}(z)) is below 1e-6 across development_validation, while the residual of a global linear fit in warped coordinates is statistically indistinguishable from noise.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Either (a) reconstruction error of the invertible warp is large, indicating the invertibility constraint is not satisfiable with the given parameter budget, (b) the warp collapses to near-identity (jacobian ~ I) and the model reduces to a plain linear operator, or (c) multi-step rollout error matches the linear baseline within noise.
risks: Normalizing flows on 52D with affine coupling layers may need careful initialization and may be unstable to train; risk of non-invertibility if scale parameters saturate.
Alternating optimization between phi and A may oscillate; need a careful schedule.
If true dynamics are genuinely nonlinear even in some warped coordinates, the linear core assumption will fail and no warp can rescue it; in that case the warp may overfit and hurt generalization.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Distinct from Koopman embeddings with linear operator (different coordinates), from RKHS operator-valued kernels (no explicit coordinate warp, no invertibility), from nonlinear lifting (non-invertible, higher-dim), and from divergence-free or symplectic coordinates (rigid physics priors vs. learnable data-driven warp). It is conceptually closest to normalising-flow state-space models, but here the linear core is global and 52D, and the warp is explicitly invertible rather than a probabilistic flow.

hypotheses.name: State-dependent stochastic forcing with structured mean and learned multiplicative innovation
hypotheses.scientific_question: Is a substantial fraction of the irreducible error in latent prediction actually aleatoric (state-conditional stochasticity) rather than model-form error, and can it be captured by a state-dependent multiplicative noise term on top of a structured deterministic mean?
hypotheses.mechanism: The latent dynamics are modelled as a discrete-time SDE on the same 52D POD coordinates: z_{t+1} = A z_t + u(z_t) + B(z_t) xi_t, where A is a small structured mean operator, u(z) is a low-rank state-dependent correction, B(z) is a state-dependent gain (e.g. B(z) = diag(sigma_i(z_i)) with a small neural net mapping each coordinate to its own scale, or a low-rank factor L(z) L(z)^T), and xi_t is standard normal. At evaluation, predict the conditional mean ẑ_{t+1} = A z_t + u(z_t) and report predictive variance diag(B(z_t) B(z_t)^T). Training minimizes a Gaussian negative log-likelihood, not just MSE, so the noise model is calibrated.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: z_{t+1} ~ N(mu(z_t), Sigma(z_t)) with mu(z) = A z + U phi(z) (U is 52 x r, phi is an r-dim feature map, r small) and Sigma(z) = L(z) L(z)^T + eps I, L(z) = softplus(W_L z + b_L) with W_L of shape k x 52 (k small, e.g. 8). Loss: sum_t [ 0.5 (z_{t+1} - mu(z_t))^T Sigma^{-1}(z_t) (z_{t+1} - mu(z_t)) + 0.5 log det Sigma(z_t) ] evaluated on development_train only. Hyperparameters selected on development_validation.
hypotheses.motivation: Every prior candidate was a deterministic predictor. Even those that modelled residual corrections (H_fallback_residual, C002_H03 sparse symbolic + residual) treated the residual as a deterministic function of z_t. In many fluid flows, the unresolved subgrid-scale forcing has a magnitude that depends on the local state (e.g., larger variance in transition or shear regions). A multiplicative-noise model can capture this and also provides calibrated predictive variance, which is valuable both scientifically (identifying regions of unpredictability) and for downstream use. This is genuinely different from the info-theoretic nonlinearity test (C004_H02), which asked whether nonlinearity is needed; here we assume both nonlinearity and stochasticity are needed and ask whether the noise structure is state-dependent.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: Prior deterministic operators (linear, structured linear, graph-block, RKHS, equivariance, non-modal) all try to fit a one-to-one map. If the underlying process has state-conditional noise, a deterministic model will necessarily average, producing state-dependent bias that looks like a model-form error. By introducing state-conditional variance and training under a likelihood that accounts for it, the deterministic mean can be a much better predictor of the conditional expectation even if the operator alone is simple. This separates aleatoric from epistemic error in a way no prior candidate did.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If the hypothesis is true: (i) the learned B(z) will be small in laminar-like regions and large in regions where the global linear operator had high error, (ii) the standardized residuals (z_{t+1} - mu(z_t)) elementwise divided by sqrt(Sigma_ii(z_t)) will be approximately standard normal and temporally uncorrelated on development_validation, whereas the raw residuals of a deterministic global linear operator will be heteroscedastic and structured, and (iii) calibrated predictive intervals at, say, 95% will have approximately 95% empirical coverage on development_validation, while a deterministic model's residual-variance proxy will mis-cover.
minimum_experiment: Train on development_train with Gaussian NLL; tune (r, k, eps) on development_validation by held-out NLL.
Compute standardized one-step residuals on development_validation; test for normality and autocorrelation.
Compute empirical coverage of 1-sigma and 2-sigma predictive intervals stratified by latent state region (e.g., by energy quartile or by recurrence indicator).
Compare multi-step rollout RMSE of the conditional mean against a deterministic global linear operator baseline (matched parameter count).
Compare NLL against a constant-variance Gaussian baseline to verify that the state-dependence of Sigma is needed.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: Standardized residuals are approximately Gaussian and serially uncorrelated, predictive intervals achieve nominal coverage on development_validation, Sigma(z) varies systematically with state (e.g., correlates with local linear-operator error), and the conditional mean beats the deterministic baseline on multi-step rollout RMSE on development_validation.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Sigma(z) collapses to a constant, NLL matches the constant-variance baseline within noise, standardized residuals remain non-Gaussian or autocorrelated, and the conditional mean does not improve over a plain deterministic structured operator on development_validation.
risks: If the runner contract is strictly deterministic at evaluation, the predictive variance may be discarded and the benefit is invisible; we would then need to also report the conditional mean RMSE.
State-dependent Gaussian noise is a parametric assumption; if the true noise is heavy-tailed or correlated across coordinates, the simple L(z)L(z)^T form may mis-cover.
If the system is in fact low-noise deterministic, adding a stochastic term may slightly hurt mean prediction due to variance-bias trade-off; we should report a balanced comparison.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Distinct from deterministic structured operators (no noise model), from sparse-symbolic+residual (deterministic residual, not stochastic), and from the information-theoretic nonlinearity test (C004_H02), which only tests for nonlinearity. It is also distinct from non-modal transient growth (C004_H01), which is a diagnostic of linear operator structure, not a predictive model with stochastic innovation.

hypotheses.name: Rotational-dissipative spectral decomposition with band-wise skew/symmetric split
hypotheses.scientific_question: Are the latent dynamics best described as a single structured linear operator A = A_rot + A_diss + A_band where A_rot is skew-symmetric (energy-preserving rotation between mode pairs), A_diss is symmetric negative semi-definite (energy dissipation concentrated on selected spectral bands), and A_band is a low-rank coupling across spectral bands - and is this structural prior better than either a fully free linear operator (C003_H02) or a strictly energy-preserving symplectic operator (C002_H01)?
hypotheses.mechanism: Decompose the 52D operator as A = S - D + U V^T, where S is skew-symmetric (S^T = -S), D is diagonal with non-negative entries d_i (so -D is symmetric negative semi-definite), and U V^T is a low-rank cross-band coupling (rank r small, e.g. 4). The 52D coordinates are partitioned into spectral bands (e.g. 4 bands of 13 modes each by POD energy rank) and a within-band skew-symmetric block encourages oscillatory coupling of similar-frequency modes, while dissipation is allowed to differ per band. All entries are real; A is a single 52x52 matrix, no residual, no memory, no input history. Trained on development_train, hyperparameters (r, number of bands, band partition) selected on development_validation.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: A = S - D + U V^T, with S = blockdiag(S_1, ..., S_B) where each S_b is b_b x b_b skew-symmetric (b_b = 52/B for equal bands), D = diag(d_1, ..., d_52) with d_i >= 0 enforced by softplus, U in R^{52 x r}, V in R^{52 x r}, r in {2,4,8}. Total parameter count comparable to a fully free dense 52x52 operator. Prediction: z_{t+1} = A z_t. Loss: MSE on development_train. The structural constraints are soft (S skew-symmetric by parameterization S = (M - M^T)/2, not by hard projection at every step), so the model can in principle approach a free operator if the data demands it, but is regularized toward the structured family.
hypotheses.motivation: Fluid ROMs typically have both oscillatory (vortex shedding, wave-like) and dissipative (viscous decay) components, and the dissipation is not uniform across POD bands - higher modes are usually more dissipative. A free dense operator has too many degrees of freedom and tends to either overfit or to invent unphysical dynamics; a strictly symplectic operator (C002_H01) forbids dissipation entirely, which is inappropriate for viscous flow. A single structured operator with explicit skew/symmetric split and band-wise dissipation is a physically motivated middle ground that has not been tried. It is also genuinely different from the energy-band-structured sparse operator (C003_H02), which used sparsity across bands but did not impose the skew/symmetric structural split; and different from the energy-decomposed linear+residual model (C003_H03), which used a separate residual term rather than embedding the structure inside A.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: C002_H01 (symplectic) failed infrastructure-wise, but if evaluated, it would systematically miss viscous dissipation. C003_H02 (band-sparse) imposed only sparsity, which is too weak a prior; the energy of a free 52x52 matrix is not concentrated in a band-sparse pattern in general. C003_H03 (linear+residual) split the operator into a linear part and a nonlinear residual; this conflates dissipation with nonlinearity, because dissipation can be expressed either as a symmetric negative part of a linear operator or as a nonlinear correction, and the two parameterizations have different inductive biases. This hypothesis keeps the operator linear and complete (no residual, no memory) and instead regularizes its structure, allowing us to test whether the structural prior itself is the issue, separate from any nonlinearity question.
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: If true: (i) on development_validation, the multi-step rollout RMSE of this structured A will be lower than that of a fully free 52x52 operator at the same parameter count, because the structural prior matches the physics, (ii) the fitted D will be larger for higher-POD-index modes and smaller for low-index modes (a natural dissipation ordering), and (iii) the singular values of S will be clustered (indicating band-structured rotation) rather than spread. (iv) Energy E_t = ||z_t||^2 will decay approximately exponentially in laminar regions, with rate given by the leading eigenvalue of -D, and the rate should differ systematically between regimes.
minimum_experiment: Train A on development_train with the structural parameterization; sweep B in {2,4,8} and r in {2,4,8} on development_validation.

Compare against (a) a fully free dense 52x52 linear operator at matched parameter count, (b) the strict symplectic variant (D=0, U V^T=0), and (c) the band-sparse variant (no skew/symmetric split, just sparsity across bands).
Inspect the fitted D: is it monotone non-decreasing in POD mode index? Compare to energy decay rates estimated directly from development_validation trajectories.
Measure rollout RMSE at horizons 1, 5, 10, 20 steps and check whether the structured operator degrades more gracefully than the free operator.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: Structured A beats both the free operator and the strict symplectic variant on multi-step rollout RMSE on development_validation; fitted dissipation rates increase with mode index; energy decay in laminar regions is well-captured by -D.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Free operator matches or beats the structured A; fitted D is not monotone in mode index; strict symplectic variant performs comparably, indicating dissipation is not the dominant missing structure.
risks: If the dynamics are actually non-normal with strong non-modal amplification, the skew/symmetric split may not be the right structural prior; the leading eigenvalues may be misleading.
If the partition into spectral bands is not the right one (e.g., modes are not band-structured), the block-diagonal S may be overly restrictive; we mitigate this with the U V^T coupling term.

If the dynamics are regime-dependent (as several prior candidates assumed), a single global structured A will underperform even with these priors; that result would still be informative because it would localize the failure to the single-operator assumption rather than the structure class.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: Distinct from C002_H01 (no dissipation, no cross-band coupling), from C003_H02 (only sparsity, no skew/symmetric split), from C003_H03 (no residual; structure is inside A), from the graph-block model (cycle 6 H3) (no explicit skew/symmetric structure, blocks defined by learned partition rather than spectral bands), and from the non-modal transient growth diagnostic (C004_H01) (which was a diagnostic, not a predictive model).

hypothesis.name: Rotational-dissipative spectral decomposition with band-wise skew/symmetric split
hypothesis.scientific_question: Are the latent dynamics best described as a single structured linear operator A = A_rot + A_diss + A_band where A_rot is skew-symmetric (energy-preserving rotation between mode pairs), A_diss is symmetric negative semi-definite (energy dissipation concentrated on selected spectral bands), and A_band is a low-rank coupling across spectral bands - and is this structural prior better than either a fully free linear operator (C003_H02) or a strictly energy-preserving symplectic operator (C002_H01)?
hypothesis.mechanism: Decompose the 52D operator as A = S - D + U V^T, where S is skew-symmetric (S^T = -S), D is diagonal with non-negative entries d_i (so -D is symmetric negative semi-definite), and U V^T is a low-rank cross-band coupling (rank r small, e.g. 4). The 52D coordinates are partitioned into spectral bands (e.g. 4 bands of 13 modes each by POD energy rank) and a within-band skew-symmetric block encourages oscillatory coupling of similar-frequency modes, while dissipation is allowed to differ per band. All entries are real; A is a single 52x52 matrix, no residual, no memory, no input history. Trained on development_train, hyperparameters (r, number of bands, band partition) selected on development_validation.
hypothesis.mathematical_form: A = S - D + U V^T, with S = blockdiag(S_1, ..., S_B) where each S_b is b_b x b_b skew-symmetric (b_b = 52/B for equal bands), D = diag(d_1, ..., d_52) with d_i >= 0 enforced by softplus, U in R^{52 x r}, V in R^{52 x r}, r in {2,4,8}. Total parameter count comparable to a fully free dense 52x52 operator. Prediction: z_{t+1} = A z_t. Loss: MSE on development_train. The structural constraints are soft (S skew-symmetric by parameterization S = (M - M^T)/2, not by hard projection at every step), so the model can in principle approach a free operator if the data demands it, but is regularized toward the structured family.
hypothesis.motivation: Fluid ROMs typically have both oscillatory (vortex shedding, wave-like) and dissipative (viscous decay) components, and the dissipation is not uniform across POD bands - higher modes are usually more dissipative. A free dense operator has too many degrees of freedom and tends to either overfit or to invent unphysical dynamics; a strictly symplectic operator (C002_H01) forbids dissipation entirely, which is inappropriate for viscous flow. A single structured operator with explicit skew/symmetric split and band-wise dissipation is a physically motivated middle ground that has not been tried. It is also genuinely different from the energy-band-structured sparse operator (C003_H02), which used sparsity across bands but did not impose the skew/symmetric structural split; and different from the energy-decomposed linear+residual model (C003_H03), which used a separate residual term rather than embedding the structure inside A.
hypothesis.explanation_of_previous_failure: C002_H01 (symplectic) failed infrastructure-wise, but if evaluated, it would systematically miss viscous dissipation. C003_H02 (band-sparse) imposed only sparsity, which is too weak a prior; the energy of a free 52x52 matrix is not concentrated in a band-sparse pattern in general. C003_H03 (linear+residual) split the operator into a linear part and a nonlinear residual; this conflates dissipation with nonlinearity, because dissipation can be expressed either as a symmetric negative part of a linear operator or as a nonlinear correction, and the two parameterizations have different inductive biases. This hypothesis keeps the operator linear and complete (no residual, no memory) and instead regularizes its structure, allowing us to test whether the structural prior itself is the issue, separate from any nonlinearity question.
hypothesis.distinguishing_prediction: If true: (i) on development_validation, the multi-step rollout RMSE of this structured A will be lower than that of a fully free 52x52 operator at the same parameter count, because the structural prior matches the physics, (ii) the fitted D will be larger for higher-POD-index modes and smaller for low-index modes (a natural dissipation ordering), and (iii) the singular values of S will be clustered (indicating band-structured rotation) rather than spread. (iv) Energy E_t = ||z_t||^2 will decay approximately exponentially in laminar regions, with rate given by the leading eigenvalue of -D, and the rate should differ systematically between regimes.
minimum_experiment: Train A on development_train with the structural parameterization; sweep B in {2,4,8} and r in {2,4,8} on development_validation.

Compare against (a) a fully free dense 52x52 linear operator at matched parameter count, (b) the strict symplectic variant (D=0, U V^T=0), and (c) the band-sparse variant (no skew/symmetric split, just sparsity across bands).
Inspect the fitted D: is it monotone non-decreasing in POD mode index? Compare to energy decay rates estimated directly from development_validation trajectories.
Measure rollout RMSE at horizons 1, 5, 10, 20 steps and check whether the structured operator degrades more gracefully than the free operator.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_true: Structured A beats both the free operator and the strict symplectic variant on multi-step rollout RMSE on development_validation; fitted dissipation rates increase with mode index; energy decay in laminar regions is well-captured by -D.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_false: Free operator matches or beats the structured A; fitted D is not monotone in mode index; strict symplectic variant performs comparably, indicating dissipation is not the dominant missing structure.
risks: If the dynamics are actually non-normal with strong non-modal amplification, the skew/symmetric split may not be the right structural prior; the leading eigenvalues may be misleading.
If the partition into spectral bands is not the right one (e.g., modes are not band-structured), the block-diagonal S may be overly restrictive; we mitigate this with the U V^T coupling term.

If the dynamics are regime-dependent (as several prior candidates assumed), a single global structured A will underperform even with these priors; that result would still be informative because it would localize the failure to the single-operator assumption rather than the structure class.
hypothesis.relation_to_existing_methods: Distinct from C002_H01 (no dissipation, no cross-band coupling), from C003_H02 (only sparsity, no skew/symmetric split), from C003_H03 (no residual; structure is inside A), from the graph-block model (cycle 6 H3) (no explicit skew/symmetric structure, blocks defined by learned partition rather than spectral bands), and from the non-modal transient growth diagnostic (C004_H01) (which was a diagnostic, not a predictive model).
